recipes.name: Jewish Apple Cake from Bubba's Recipe Box
ingredients_raw: 5 large Rome Beauty apples, peeled, cored, and chopped

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan.

Mix cinnamon, 3/4 cup of sugar, and apples in a bowl; set aside. Combine flour, salt, and baking powder in a separate bowl. Beat eggs and 2 cups of sugar with an electric mixer until fluffy. Pour in flour mixture alternately with the oil. Beat in orange juice and vanilla until smooth and thoroughly mixed. Pour half of the batter into the prepared pan. Layer half of the apples on top. Pour remaining batter over, then finish by topping with the rest of the apples.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 1 hour and 30 minutes to 1 hour and 45 minutes. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before removing to cool completely on a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Jewish Apple Cake from Bubba's Recipe Box
raw_recipe.description: This moist Jewish apple cake, with layers of tender apples sweetened with sugar and cinnamon, makes a crowd-pleasing dessert for holiday potlucks.

review.reviewBody: Wow - this is one awesome Jewish Apple Cake! And it's definitely a crowd pleaser as the submitter states. It sweet, moist, rises beautifully and is absolutely delicious. I didn't have Rome Beauty apples, so I used a combination of apples that I had on hand. Other than that, I would change a thing with this recipe. Apparently since this recipe has been handed down and made for over 37 years - if it ain't broke, don't fix it! All I had to do with this after it cooled, was to dust it with a little confectioners' sugar as if this beautiful cake needed anything else. Thanks Janyce for a wonderful recipe that I hope many more people try, they'll be glad they did!

Heavenly! To make it healthy version: I replace 1 c oil with 1 c unsweetened applesauce; use 1 c egg beaters instead of 4 whole eggs; reduce white sugar by 1/2 c. For flavor, try replacing the 3/4 c white sugar with brown sugar to mix with the cinnamon and up the cinnamon to 4 tsp - also sprinkle some raisins or dates or dried cranberries for variety. Whole house smelled wonderful. I think with the healthy changes, this would make a nice breakfast addition.

Very flavorful cake. I made the following changes: I reduced the sugar by 1/4 cup and used white and brown sugar in equal parts. I used about 4 oz of sour cream in the batter with the oil. I added white raisins to the apple mixture. I baked in two loaf pans and it took 1 hour 20 minutes to bake. 

I made a maple glaze for the top: 1/2 cup powdered sugar, 1 tablespoon of heavy cream, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon. Mix well until smooth, adding more heavy cream as necessary to achieve a pouring consistency. 

I shared with friends and it got rave reviews. The second loaf, without the glaze, made a wonderful breakfast bread.

My 13yo daughter followed the recipe as written, but added a brown sugar glaze. (Melt 1/4c butter in a saucepan. Add 1/2 c brown sugar and cook 2 minutes, whisking constantly. Continue whisking and add 1/4 c milk. Bring to a boil. Remove pan from heat and add 1 tsp vanilla. Add 1 2/3 c powdered sugar in 1/3 cup increments, whisking after each addition.)

It was a good cake, but not great. I substituted Gala apples for the Rome apples because Romes weren't available. Next time I make it I'm going to add at least a teaspoon of cinnamon to the batter, not just to mix with the apples. I will also bake it for 10 minutes less than the recipe calls for. My tube pan is dark and thick and my cake was overdone at 90 minutes. It started smelling "done" at 70 minutes, and I should have probably only baked it 80 minutes. I also made a glaze out of the remaining cinnamon sugar mixture left over from the apples (and added more cinnamon), which I think gave the cake an extra oomph.

Absolutely phenomenal recipe! I just got a new fridge yesterday, and in unloading and reloading, I came upon a bag of cranberries that really needed to be used - NOW. So I first made cranberry sauce out of them, cooled it, and used it in this cake, in place of half the apples. I scraped 1/3 of the batter in the pan, topped with the cranberry sauce, put in another 1/3 of the batter, topped with the halved apple mixture, scraped in the remaining batter. The flavor is sensational, the texture super moist. Aside from the cranberries standing in for half the apples, I cut the flour back to 2-3/4 cup. I baked it for only 85 minutes. I checked on it at about 45 minutes, and it appeared to be browning early. So I placed a piece of foil on top for the remainder of the baking time. It came out with a nice, crunchy crust on top. I glazed it with a lovely caramel rum glaze: 3 Tb butter, 2 Tb brown sugar, 2 Tb white sugar, 1/4 tsp vanilla, 1 tsp dark rum, 2 Tb whipping cream, combined in a small sauce pan over medium-low heat, until it comes to a simmer. Continue to simmer for 3 minutes. Brush over the warm cake, right after you remove it from the pan. It's not a lot of glaze, but it's quite flavorful, just enough to point up the cake's ingredients to perfection and to impart a lovely sheen. BTW, I will try making it with only apples the next time. Yes, the cranberries and glaze were a little difference, but the cake flavor and texture remained unchanged, and gotta say, they're stellar.

This was a wonderful cake. I always have to change recipes just a little to make it my own. Added some cinnamon to the batter and made a streusal topping with oatmeal, brown sugar, cinnamon and some butter. Baked it in a 9 x 13 pan for 1 hour. Had some really tart apples and was afraid they might be too tart, but they weren't. Served with homemade cinnamon ice cream and everyone loved it.

I have this exact same recipe in a cookbook my mother had written out for me a couple decades ago, just before she passed. She made this for Christmas every year for our family and I continue this tradition for mine. I macerate the apples for at least a half an hour, at most a hour, not only does this soften the apples, but I use the juice to top the cake before baking as it makes a crackling glaze. This is a great recipe and I would recommend making this. Also I used either Fiji apples or Golden delicious apples using the Golden apples makes for a softer apple in the cake when baking which is a huge hit. The Fiji are nice but remain a little firm when baked but either are fantastic!

Came out beautiful. I did some extra prep. I lined the bottom of my tube pan with parchment paper. I also omitted the orange juice from the batter. I instead squeezed a fresh lemon and orange into a bowl and added the instructed sugar and cinnamon with the sliced apples and let the apple slices marinate in the mixture. I drained off the marinade and lightly squeezed the apple slices before layering into the batter. I cut the cake in half to easily remove from the pan and and plated the halves together as one whole cake. Couldn't see the seam as to where I cut it with all of the beautifully browned apple slices on the top of the cake. This was a test to make sure I could make this cake for a party I am going to. Success!

This was my first ever Apple Cake I made for my husband's birthday and I envisioned it looking like some pictures I've seen. So I decided to melt some butter to coat bottom of bundt pan, sprinkled about 1/4 cup of Brown sugar over that and then layered some thin apple slices on top of that. I then continued the recipe as directed. I couldn't be more happier about a cake! Wish I could share the photo, it looked magazine worthy! Lol - and My husband loved it! He even said it was the best Apple Cake he ever had (including his moms!) 
Our family devoured it! I am passing this along to family and friends!

Perfect! I have been making this for my kids for years now same recipe just only using 2cups apples and different method of mixing. Used this method with 4 large apples 2 tsp cinnamon and it was sooo good. Not dry at all and very delicate . Will adjust my recipe to this, happy to see it here. Never knew the name .

Made as written (though with whatever apples I had). A huge hit! My friends suggested more cinnamon or more apples but remarked over how moist it was. I had to bake longer than the recipe suggests and also cranked it to 375 for 10 minutes (which may have resulted in a beautiful caramelization on top).

This is your basic Jewish apple cake recipe that I've been making for many years myself. It's delicious! It's fairly easy to make. The reason I don't make it often is because it has a cup of oil in it (!!!!). But it's worth every bite! Oh and one more thing...it's not Bubba! It's Bubby or Bubbie
Very easy! Always a big hit.

I mix the cake batter with the apples at the end and pour into a pan together instead of laying them. Also needs more cinnamon for my taste. I used a 9 by 13 pan and added a each apple. I used Granny Smith and Johnathan apples like the tart favor.

I've been baking Jewish Apple Cakes forever. This is a good basic recipe, and in it of itself, it is delicious. But, of course, being an experienced cook, I have to stick my foot in it. I used apple juice instead of orange juice. I also used 3/8ths cup white sugar and 3/8ths cup brown sugar, along with 1/2 Tablespoon of cinnamon, with the apples and maserated for 24 to 48 hours,
I use different apples and it still makes a top tier cake.
I made a carmely glaze. Added some nutmeg and a little extra cinnamon.

First time making this and it was a success! I doubled the recipe because I had so many apples. I didn't have a tube pan and it was late, so I used two loaf pans and a bundt pan (smaller than a 10 cup). It took about an hour to cook. They did stick in the bundt can and the one loaf pan, next time I'll grease it better OR get a tube pan and try that. Thank you!

My mom used to make Jewish apple cake when I was a kid, this was my first time making it and it was perfect. Everyone loved it, the recipe was easy to follow, I'm about to make the second one in 2 weeks!
